discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Zoller and co-workers proposed in 1998 that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model with tunable parameters. In 2002 Greiner and Bloch observed the quantum phase transition from a superfluid to a Mott insulator, turning a textbook model of strongly correlated matter into a clean, controllable experiment. This launched analog quantum simulation as a field. Bloch and Greiner then developed quantum gas microscopes with single-site, single-atom resolution, which made it possible to image Mott shells, antiferromagnetic correlations, string order and entanglement in Hubbard systems directly. Their experiments are quantitative and conclusive, and they now provide benchmarks against which condensed-matter theory and numerical methods are tested, including for the doped Fermi-Hubbard model relevant to high-temperature superconductivity. Theory and experiment worked closely together here, and the result is a lasting new experimental tool for physics.
